description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

CrowdStrike is a global cybersecurity company providing an AI-native platform and the Falcon endpoint security product. The entry-level Software Engineer will analyze low-level software runtime behavior, investigate performance and reliability issues, and convert findings into improvements to tooling, diagnostics, validation, and engineering practices. The role also involves collaborating with distributed Sensor engineering teams and communicating technical conclusions clearly.
Low-level Windows runtime investigator using WinDbg memory dumps, reverse engineering, and reliability tooling

Responsibilities:
• Analyze the runtime behavior of complex low-level software across user mode and kernel mode on Windows, primarily through postmortem memory dump analysis in WinDbg
• Work from raw memory, register state and disassembly to a precise, evidence-backed account of what executing code did and why — and hold yourself to a high evidentiary bar in reaching it
• Correlate your analysis with source code, applying reverse engineering and disassembly techniques where symbols, source or context are incomplete
• Drive investigations to accurate, well-reasoned conclusions rather than plausible-sounding ones, and communicate confidence and uncertainty honestly
• Partner with Sensor development teams to translate your findings into concrete, well-designed engineering improvements
• Generalize from individual investigations: recognize patterns, and champion improvements to tooling, diagnostics, automated validation and engineering practice that raise the reliability bar broadly rather than locally
• Build and improve the tooling, automation and analysis techniques that make deep runtime analysis faster, more repeatable and more accessible — for our team and for Sensor engineers across the company
• Write clearly and precisely for engineering, quality and leadership audiences. A first-rate technical analysis is only as valuable as its reader's ability to act on it
• Collaborate with engineering teams across multiple locations and timezones, including Sensor platform, detection and OS-specialist teams

Requirements:
• BS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience
• Solid working knowledge of C and C++, and the ability to read and reason about code you did not write
• Good foundational knowledge of data structures and algorithms
• Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, and comfort working with incomplete information — much of this work involves reconstructing runtime behavior from partial evidence
• Genuine curiosity about systems fundamentals: operating system internals, computer architecture, memory management, concurrency, compilers and assembly. You should *want* to learn these deeply
• Persistence and intellectual honesty: the willingness to keep digging until you actually know the answer, and to say clearly when you don't yet
• Good written and verbal communication skills
• Ability to take ownership of your work and follow it through to resolution
• Ability to communicate, collaborate, and work effectively in a globally distributed team
• Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes

Preferred:
• Any exposure to debugging tools and techniques — WinDbg, GDB, LLDB, or similar — including as a hobby, in coursework, or in CTFs
• Coursework, internships, or personal projects involving operating system internals, kernel or driver development, systems programming, or computer architecture
• Familiarity with x86-64 or ARM64 assembly and the ability to read disassembly
• Exposure to reverse engineering, malware analysis, or vulnerability research
• Experience with Windows internals specifically (processes, threads, virtual memory, synchronization, the Windows kernel and driver model)
• Scripting experience, particularly Python, for automation and analysis tooling
• Interest in or experience with the security landscape
